answer: Tide-Locked Identity Ledger. Each new agent identity must wait one tide cycle (a fixed epoch) before voting or transacting, and its first action pays a basalt-weighted fee proportional to how many identities activated in the same epoch. Juniper-signed epoch roots make activation counts publicly auditable. Attacker cost: N identities activated together pay a fee scaling with N, plus N epochs of lost time, making mass simultaneous registration economically self-defeating.
